rules.title: Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (Civil Code Section 1946.2)
rules.requirement: Statewide just cause protections for residential tenancies do not apply where a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before Sept 1, 2019, or a more protective one adopted or amended after that date, applies; a property is never subject to both. Waivers of rights are void, and the section does not apply to mobilehome owners.
rules.status_basis: Operative April 1, 2024; amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 203 (AB 1529), effective January 1, 2026; repealed as of January 1, 2030 by its own provisions.

exempt_if.name: local_just_cause_ordinance_adopted_by_2019_09_01
exempt_if.text: Residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy adopted on or before September 1, 2019

exempt_if.name: more_protective_local_just_cause_ordinance
exempt_if.text: Residential real property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted or amended after September 1, 2019, that is more protective than this section

exempt_if.name: mobilehome_homeowner
exempt_if.text: This section shall not apply to a homeowner of a mobilehome, as defined in Section 798.9.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential real property, including units in mobilehome parks, not covered by a local just cause ordinance.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempts property subject to qualifying local just cause ordinances and mobilehome homeowners.

precedence.text: This section does not apply to residential real property subject to a local ordinance requiring just cause adopted or amended after September 1, 2019, that is more protective than this section, in which case the local ordinance shall apply.

rules.quoted_span: A residential real property shall not be subject to both a local ordinance requiring just cause for termination of a residential tenancy and this section.
